data.text: Framer Motion is a production-ready motion library for React. It provides gestures, layout animations, and exit animations.

data.title: Framer Motion animation

data.text: Motion (formerly Framer Motion) animates any HTML or SVG element by swapping the element for its `motion.` counterpart and passing an `animate` prop. The props `initial`, `animate`, `exit`, and `transition` describe the states, and gestures such as `whileHover` and `whileTap` attach directly to the element.

data.title: Fade, slide, and hover

data.text: A shared `layout` prop animates an element between two layout states automatically, which is how a card position changes without measuring anything. `AnimatePresence` keeps an exiting element in the tree long enough to play its `exit` animation, which is what makes removal from a list feel smooth.

data.title: Animated list removal
Interview angle: animate transform and opacity
data.text: Motion makes it easy to animate anything, but only `transform` and `opacity` are cheap: they are handled by the compositor and skip layout and paint. Animating `width` or `top` triggers layout on every frame. A strong answer mentions `prefers-reduced-motion`, because an animation that ignores it can make the app unusable for some users.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Framer Motion is the standard for React animations.
